official.description_text:
Postdoc in Resilient 6G Networking
Login and apply
School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at KTH
Job description
6G networking is supposed to cater towards new use cases, which will integrate communication and computing in novel and highly dependent ways. A new application class, summarized as the Cyber-Physical Continuum, will be enabled by 6G networks, allowing entirely new use cases with unprecedented utility to societies. Nevertheless, these new opportunities are associated with an ever-increasing complexity of future networked systems. It is commonly accepted in the academic and industrial research community that AI will play here a pivotal role in efficiently managing such future networks despite the complexity increase.
Our research group is focusing on science paving the way towards 6G networks, with a particular emphasis on the dependable Cyber-Physical Continuum. Our research agenda is supported through several leading large initiatives, where recently we have engaged on a project in the domain of resilient 6G networking. In this context we are seeking in this call postdoc candidates with the ambition to lead research in the domain of 6G, AI and resilience. Aspects such as novel threat scenarios, distributed inference, AI RAN and resilience play a significant role in this context. The position involves collaborations within our research group as well as with other research groups from different disciplines and universities. It will also comprise collaborations with industrial partners.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Research expertise
Teaching abilities
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Collaboration abilities
Independence
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
A track record in theoretical or experimental 6G research, for instance with respect to, ultra-reliability, low latency, performance prediction, distributed inference or related areas.
Strong background in machine learning is a plus.
Team leadership skills, or an interest in developing them.
Strong communication skills (both orally and in writing)
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH's School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science researching 6G networking resilience, AI-driven network management, and the Cyber-Physical Continuum, with emphasis on distributed inference, threat scenarios, and ultra-reliability.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is fundamentally a telecommunications and distributed systems research role centred on 6G, AI for network optimization, and cyber-physical systems. The researcher's domains (immersive learning, spatial cognition, collaborative XR, wayfinding, user studies, gamification) do not align. 6G networking is infrastructure-layer research; no mention of user experience, human interaction, learning outcomes, or immersive applications.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position mentions machine learning and collaboration across disciplines, which are transferable concepts. However, the methods are theoretical/computational (distributed inference, AI, network resilience)—not experimental user studies, design science, or HCI evaluation. Researcher's strength in qualitative design evaluation and user-centred validation is not needed.

growth_value.rationale: This position would develop skills in 6G, distributed AI, and network security—none of which align with the target identity (human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, collaborative design). Would not close gaps relevant to doctoral HCI research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is prestigious with strong funding. However, the research community (6G, AI systems, telecommunications) differs substantially from target HCI groups at Aalto and TU Delft. Limited value for building a human-centred XR research network or establishing connections in the target domain.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress); position requires completed doctoral degree. Not yet eligible.
Position may require security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act; eligibility depends on nationality—not stated in profile.
risks: Domain mismatch: telecommunications and distributed systems engineering ≠ human-centred XR/HCI.
Researcher would need to acquire machine learning and 6G expertise from scratch; no demonstrated background.
Pure ML/AI systems research, which is on the excluded directions list ('pure-machine-learning-algorithms').
Not yet PhD-eligible; position is postdoctoral.
No user-centred or HCI component; research outputs would not advance human-centred immersive systems goals.
Security clearance requirement may introduce barriers.
